provenance.generatedBy: claude-opus-5-5 · Field Kit v2 Prompt A batch
provenance.notes: Edu family batch. Season-driven category: recital and fall registration set the timing. Ranges are planning figures, not quotes.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Recital date and venue, dress rehearsal schedule, costume fee and due date, ticket sales, photo and video order info, and what each class performs
pageStructurePlus.why: Recital questions flood a dance studio every spring. Parents judge how organised the studio is by how easy the recital information is to find.

pageStructurePlus.section: Dancewear and shoe list by class
pageStructurePlus.contains: Leotard colour, tights, ballet slippers, tap shoes and jazz shoes for each class level, hair rules for ballet, and where families can buy them
pageStructurePlus.why: A parent enrolling a five-year-old in ballet wants to know what to buy before the first class. Getting it wrong is the first frustration.

pageStructurePlus.contains: How the studio places a ten-year-old beginner or a transfer dancer, the placement class, and the ballet, jazz, tap and hip hop levels explained
pageStructurePlus.why: Older beginners and dancers switching studios worry about landing in a class of little kids. A clear placement path keeps them enrolling.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Audition dates, rehearsal hours, competition weekends, costume and travel costs, solo and duet fees, and the commitment expected from families
pageStructurePlus.why: Competition families give up most weekends of the season. They pick the studio whose team expectations are written down before the audition.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Adult ballet, tap, hip hop and ballroom basics, drop-in rules, class cards, and what a nervous first-timer should expect
pageStructurePlus.why: Adults fill the evening studio slots kids can't use, and they only book when the page says beginners are welcome.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Rentable dance rooms by size, floor type, mirrors and sound system, hourly rates, and booking rules for rehearsals, choreographers and photo shoots
pageStructurePlus.why: Empty daytime studio rooms are money left on the floor. Choreographers and wedding couples book rehearsal space online or not at all.

designDirections.name: Fall Registration
designDirections.bestFor: Neighbourhood dance studios that need fall and January registration more than a showcase
designDirections.headlineSample: Dance classes for kids in {City}. Fall registration is open.
designDirections.whyItFits: Teal and tangerine feel like a recital programme, and the humanist type stays friendly to parents scanning class levels on a phone.

designDirections.name: First Position
designDirections.bestFor: Family dance studios with ballet, tap, jazz and hip hop by age, and a busy recital season
designDirections.headlineSample: Ballet, tap, jazz and hip hop for {City} dancers
designDirections.whyItFits: The family combo. Sky Kite's light sky ground and rounded type suit little dancers, and the card stack sorts classes by age and style.

designDirections.name: Ballet Academy
designDirections.bestFor: Pre-professional ballet academies and competition studios with a strong company
designDirections.whyItFits: Rosewood's Didone display is the type of a ballet programme, and the blush ground lets a full-bleed performance shot carry the page.

openers.line: Your dance studio's Google listing has hours and a phone number but no website, so a parent searching ballet classes for a four-year-old in {City} can't see times or what to buy.
openers.hook: Open their Maps listing and confirm there is no Website button. Screenshot it for when they reply.
openers.linkLine: Here's the dance studio page that would sit behind that button: {demo-link}

openers.line: The website link for the dance studio goes to Facebook, where fall class times are a flyer post that's slipped down the page. Parents want the ballet and tap schedule in one place.
openers.hook: Tap the link and find the latest schedule or registration post. Note how far down it sits.
openers.linkLine: Every dance class by age and style, on one page: {demo-link}

openers.line: The dance studio site on your listing still advertises a recital from a past spring. Parents enrolling this fall notice the old date before the new classes.
openers.hook: Open the site and find one stale detail: an old recital, old tuition, a dead registration form. Note it.
openers.linkLine: Same dance studio, current and ready for registration: {demo-link}

openers.line: I opened your dance studio site on my phone and the class grid shrank to unreadable. Parents check ballet times on their phone between practices and pickups.
openers.hook: Only if they have a site. Load it on your phone and note what breaks. Screenshot it for when they reply.
openers.linkLine: The same dance studio, rebuilt for a phone: {demo-link}

openers.line: Registration for the dance studio looks like a printable form to drop off at the front desk. A parent ready to enrol at night has to wait until you're open.
openers.hook: Look for a PDF, a printable form or 'register in person'. If so, the angle holds.
openers.linkLine: Dance class registration that works at night: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your recital posts show beautiful costumes and full stages, and they're gone from the feed by summer. A recital page would keep showing new dance parents what the year builds to.
openers.hook: Find their most recent recital or showcase post and note the theme or a piece named.
openers.linkLine: Your recital, kept where new dance families will see it: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your Google reviews have parents describing a shy daughter who now loves the stage. That kind of dance studio review belongs next to the registration button.
openers.hook: Read their reviews and copy one phrase a parent wrote about their dancer. Quote it back if they reply.
openers.linkLine: Dance parent reviews next to the classes they describe: {demo-link}

openers.line: Fall dance registration fills the most popular ballet and hip hop slots in a few weeks. Studios with an online registration page take those spots before the phone rings.
openers.hook: Use this from late June through August, or in December for January classes. Name the season.
openers.linkLine: A fall registration page for the dance studio: {demo-link}

openers.line: Recital week brings late-night messages about costumes, call times and tickets. A recital page on the dance studio site would answer most of them before they're sent.
openers.hook: Look for recital-week comments asking about times, tickets or costumes. Note one.
openers.linkLine: A dance recital hub that answers the 11pm questions: {demo-link}

openers.line: Saw you're hiring a ballet or hip hop teacher for the dance studio. Strong teachers look at the studio's site to judge the culture before they apply.
openers.hook: Only if they posted a hiring note for teachers or front desk. Note the role.
openers.linkLine: A dance studio page with a teach-with-us section: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your dance studio rooms look empty in the daytime posts, and choreographers and wedding couples in {Neighborhood} need rehearsal space with mirrors and a sprung floor.
openers.hook: Only if they mention studio rental or have an empty-room post. Note the room or floor they show.
openers.linkLine: A dance room rental page with hourly booking: {demo-link}

openers.line: I couldn't find tuition or a costume fee for the dance classes anywhere. A parent who can't tell what a year of ballet costs tends to enrol where it's written down.
openers.hook: Check every page and post for tuition, registration and costume fees. If none show, the angle holds.
openers.linkLine: Dance tuition, registration and costume fees, written plainly: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your teachers' dance training and performing backgrounds are why parents should pick the studio, and none of it shows where a new ballet family would look.
openers.hook: Look for teacher bios, company credits or syllabus certifications in posts. Never invent a credential.
openers.linkLine: Your dance faculty next to the classes they teach: {demo-link}

openers.line: The dance studio seems to fill with returning families and their younger siblings. When a few graduate out, the new families who replace them look you up first.
openers.hook: Look for posts celebrating seniors or reviews saying 'my third daughter dancing here'. Quote it.
openers.linkLine: Where a new dance family would land: {demo-link}

openers.line: That {specific recent job} you posted is lovely. A competition piece or showcase number like that should open the dance studio's site, not sit three weeks deep in the feed.
openers.hook: Pick their newest competition, showcase or class post and name the piece or the award exactly.
openers.linkLine: That dance moment, front and centre: {demo-link}

sequence.dm1:
Hi {Owner} — that {specific recent job} you posted looked like a wonderful night for the dancers.

I looked for a site for {Business Name} and found the listing and your social pages, but no class schedule by age or a way to register online. I put together a sample dance studio page with classes by style and level, a recital hub and online registration, with marked placeholders where your photos would go.

Would you like me to send it over?
sequence.dm2:
{Owner} — following up in case my message got lost in recital and registration messages. Here's the sample dance studio site for {Business Name}: {demo-link}

It has ballet, tap, jazz and hip hop by age, a dancewear list per class, a recital hub and online registration. If it's not for you, say so and I won't message again.
sequence.call:
"Hi, is this {Owner}? I'm {Your Name}, I build websites for dance studios here in {City}. I sent you a message a couple of days ago, did it come through?"

IF NO:
"Easy to miss in registration season. Short version: I built a sample site for {Business Name} with classes by age and style, a recital hub and online registration, with marked placeholders where your photos would go. Can I email you the link to look at after classes?"

IF YES:
"What did you think?"
 → let them talk, don't fill the silence
"The build runs {Build Range}, then {Care Range} a month for hosting and schedule changes each season. For a studio your size I'd normally quote about {Build Price}."
"Can I walk you through it for ten minutes one morning before the studio opens?"

CLOSE:
"I'll send a one-page scope and a deposit invoice. We start the day it clears, and it's live before registration opens."

objections.objection: Registration is already done for this year.
objections.handler: "Then this is the right time. The site goes live quietly now, and it's ready for January classes and next fall's registration instead of being rushed into it."

objections.objection: Our studio software has a parent portal.
objections.handler: "Keep it for billing and accounts. The portal can't sell a new parent on the studio. The site explains classes, dancewear and recital, then sends them into the same portal to register."

objections.objection: A dance mom does our website for free.
objections.handler: "That's generous of her, keep her involved. I'll hand over the recital hub and registration pages. If she'd rather not do it every season, the offer stands."

objections.objection: We're full every year from returning families.
objections.handler: "Then the site is for filling the classes that aren't full, like older beginners and adult tap, and for the room rentals sitting empty in the day."

objections.objection: Recital season is too busy to think about this.
objections.handler: "Understood. I'll check back the week after the recital, when the studio goes quiet. That's when the site should get built."
"{Build Range}. For you about {Build Price}, because it's classes by age, a recital hub and online registration. A couple of new dancers for the year cover it."

email.subject: Dance studio site for {Business Name}

sequence.voicemail: "Hi {Owner}, it's {Your Name}. I build websites for dance studios in {City}, and I put together a sample one for {Business Name} with online registration and a recital page. I'll email you the link. {Your Phone}. Thanks."
sequence.takedown:
{Owner} — I'm taking the {Business Name} dance studio demo down on Friday to free up the space.

Want me to leave it up? One word is fine either way.
sequence.nurture:
Hi {Owner} — recital is a few months off and January dance classes are next. Thought of you.

The site is still here whenever you want it, with the recital hub ready to fill in, and nothing's changed on price. {demo-link} if you want another look.

bullets: Peg the build to a couple of new dancers' year of tuition, never to the size of the recital.
Price the class schedule by number of styles and levels, not by page. A big ballet, tap, jazz and hip hop grid is the real work.
The recital hub is its own line, and it should be sold before winter break so it's ready for costume deadlines.
Price room rental booking only for studios that actually rent rooms. Otherwise leave it out.
Keep monthly add-ons under one dancer's monthly tuition. Studio margins are thin after costumes and rent.
Sell registration work in spring for fall and in October for January, never in the week registration opens.

lineItems.item: Class schedule by style and level
lineItems.description: Max when the grid covers several styles and levels with filters by age, day and room, and a dancewear note on each class.
Max with rehearsal schedule by class, costume fee checklist, ticket link and a photo and video order section.

lineItems.item: Online class registration with placement question
lineItems.description: Max with sibling discounts, a placement class booking for older beginners and a costume fee acknowledgement.
Max with audition sign-up, a commitment and fee breakdown, and a competition weekend calendar.
Max with several rooms, hourly availability, deposits and rules for rehearsals and photo shoots.
Max with weekly themed camps, age groups, half and full day options and a medical and pickup form.
Max when the schedule, registration, recital hub and dancewear list are all translated.

whatElseYouSell.name: Dress rehearsal photo session
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "Shoot the dress rehearsal, not the recital, with written parent consent for every dancer shown. Better light, no audience, a full gallery for the dance studio."
whatElseYouSell.when: Spring, booked on the dress rehearsal date. Consent forms go home with the costume notes.

whatElseYouSell.name: Google profile upkeep for the dance studio
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "New class openings, recital dates and registration news on the dance studio's Google profile every week, so parents searching ballet nearby see an active studio."

whatElseYouSell.name: Review requests after recital
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "The week after recital, dance parents get a short text asking for a review while the bouquets are still on the counter."
whatElseYouSell.when: Set up by spring, so the first wave lands the week after recital.

whatElseYouSell.name: Fall and January dance registration ads
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "Local ads for kids' ballet and hip hop timed to fall and January registration, pointed at the registration page and paused once classes fill."
whatElseYouSell.when: Pitch in June for August and in November for January. Ad spend is on top.

whatElseYouSell.name: Recital programme and poster design
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "The recital programme, the lobby poster and the ticket page in one look, with every class and dancer's name spelled right."
whatElseYouSell.when: Pitch in February, deliver a month before recital.

whatElseYouSell.name: Summer dance camp campaign
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "Themed summer dance camp weeks, princess ballet to hip hop crews, announced in March so dancers sign up before the pool and sports camps fill."
whatElseYouSell.when: Pitch in February, run March through May.

whatElseYouSell.name: Monthly dance studio post planning
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "You teach, I plan the month of dance posts around class openings, costume deadlines and competition weekends."
whatElseYouSell.when: Month 3, if they say social posting falls apart during recital season.

withoutAI.route: The dancewear shop that fits your students
withoutAI.pitchLine: "The shop where your dancers buy pointe shoes and leotards has no page listing each studio's dress code. Introduce me and I'll build it."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Dancewear shops live on studio dress codes. The studio owner sends them every new family, so the introduction is warm.

withoutAI.whoPays: The photographer, at your normal rate
withoutAI.pitchLine: "The photographer who shoots your recital needs an order page by studio and class. I'll build it so parents can order from the dance studio's link."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Recital photographers work for several studios each spring, and their sales depend on parents finding the order page.

withoutAI.route: The theatre or school auditorium that hosts the recital
withoutAI.pitchLine: "The auditorium you rent for recital has no rental page for other dance studios and choirs. You can introduce me to the manager."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Venues fill weekends with recitals. A studio that rents every year is the introduction the manager listens to.

withoutAI.whoPays: Each gym, at your normal rate
withoutAI.pitchLine: "The gymnastics gym where your acro dancers also train needs the same class-by-age registration. I'll build it on the dance studio's layout."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Dance and gymnastics families overlap, and studio owners often know the gym owner personally.

withoutAI.route: Private music and voice teachers for musical theatre students
withoutAI.whoPays: Each teacher, at your normal rate
withoutAI.pitchLine: "The voice teacher your musical theatre dancers see needs a lesson booking page. Your recommendation is the whole pitch."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Musical theatre dancers need singing and acting lessons, and the dance studio is who parents ask for a name.

withoutAI.route: Wedding couples' first dance lessons and ballroom teachers
withoutAI.whoPays: The ballroom instructor, at your normal rate
withoutAI.pitchLine: "The ballroom teacher who rents your studio room for wedding first dances needs a booking page of their own. I'll build it."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Independent instructors who rent studio rooms have no site and pay from lesson income. The room rental relationship is the introduction.

withAI.route: Dress code and sizing assistant for the dancewear shop
withAI.pitchLine: "A parent names the dance studio and class, and the assistant lists the exact leotard, tights and shoes, with the shop's sizing advice."
withAI.whyItWorks: The shop answers the same dress code question for every studio in town. One studio's list proves it.

withAI.route: Photo order help desk for recital photographers
withAI.pitchLine: "Parents ask which gallery their dancer is in and how to order prints, and the assistant answers from the photographer's class lists."
withAI.whyItWorks: Recital photographers get swamped for three weeks a year. One season of fewer emails pays for it.

withAI.route: Rental enquiry assistant for the recital venue
withAI.pitchLine: "Dance studios and choirs asking about open weekend dates, stage size and tech fees get answers and a hold request any time."
withAI.whyItWorks: Venues lose bookings to slow replies, and every hold request has a clear value.

withAI.route: Class placement assistant for gymnastics gyms
withAI.pitchLine: "Gym parents describe their child's skills, and the assistant suggests the right class level and books an evaluation."
withAI.whyItWorks: It's the dance studio's placement logic reconfigured, sold through an owner who shares families.

withAI.route: Lesson booking assistant for voice teachers
withAI.pitchLine: "Musical theatre parents ask about audition prep and open lesson times, and the voice teacher's assistant books them in."
withAI.whyItWorks: Solo teachers miss messages while teaching. A small monthly fee is less than one lesson.

withAI.route: First dance planner for ballroom instructors
withAI.pitchLine: "Engaged couples share their song and wedding date, and the planner suggests a lesson package and books the first session."
withAI.whyItWorks: Wedding lessons are seasonal and impulsive. Capturing the enquiry the night they ask is the whole sale.

softwareAI.name: Costume fee and deadline reminders
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Dance parents get a text before each costume fee and measurement deadline, so the front desk stops chasing payments in March."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2, before costumes are ordered. Needs the costume fee schedule and parent contact list.

softwareAI.name: Online registration with sibling and multi-class pricing
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Parents enrol two dancers in four classes and the price works itself out, discounts included, without a front-desk calculator."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: At build or before the next registration. Needs their tuition table, discounts and registration fee.

softwareAI.name: Recital ticket sales and seating
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Recital tickets sold online by show, with reserved seating and family limits, so nobody camps outside the studio on ticket day."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3, a few months before recital. Needs the venue seating map and ticket rules.

softwareAI.name: Dance parent DM responder
softwareAI.pitchLine: "'What should my four-year-old wear to ballet' and 'is there room in hip hop' get an answer in seconds from the dance studio's own schedule."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2. Needs the class schedule, dress code and tuition, updated every season. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Trial dance class follow-up
softwareAI.pitchLine: "A child who tried a dance class gets a note to the parent that evening and a registration link two days later, before the excitement fades."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Day 30. Needs their trial class rules and registration access.

softwareAI.name: Recital rehearsal schedule builder
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Every class's rehearsal slot, stage call time and costume change, built once and sent to each dance family as their own schedule."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4, before recital planning starts. Needs the running order and class rosters.

softwareAI.name: Dance studio phone receptionist
softwareAI.pitchLine: "While every room has a class in it, the dance studio phone still gets answered, the question handled and the trial class booked."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3, once they trust you. Needs the schedule, dress code, policies and registration access. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Costume inventory and sizing sheet
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Every dancer's measurements, costume size and order status in one list, so the wrong size isn't discovered at dress rehearsal."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4, before costume orders. Needs the costume list per class and measurement records.

softwareAI.name: Review reply drafts for the dance studio
softwareAI.pitchLine: "After recital, dozens of dance reviews arrive at once. Each one gets a thank-you drafted for the studio owner to approve from the lobby."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2, alongside the review requests. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Caption writer for recital and competition posts
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Post the competition result or the recital number, and a caption in the studio's voice with the piece and choreographer named is ready to approve."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2. Needs past captions and the studio's rule on naming dancers. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Studio room rental calendar
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Open dance rooms show by the hour, renters pay up front and the calendar blocks around your own class schedule automatically."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3, only for studios renting rooms. Needs room list, rates and house rules.

softwareAI.name: Re-enrolment reminder for next season
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Current dance families get first pick of fall classes with a reminder before open registration, so returning dancers don't lose their spot."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4, timed a few weeks ahead of fall registration. Needs current rosters and next season's schedule.

softwareAI.name: Choreography notes assistant for teachers
softwareAI.pitchLine: "A teacher speaks the counts and formations after rehearsal, and the assistant writes tidy choreography notes a substitute can follow."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 5, for studios with several teachers. Needs teacher approval on every note. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Competition team fee and travel ledger
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Which dancers are entered in which competition, what each family owes for solos and travel, and who has paid, in one ledger."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 5, only for studios with a competition team. Needs the competition calendar and fee rules.

softwareAI.name: Class level placement quiz
softwareAI.pitchLine: "A parent or adult beginner answers questions about age and dance experience, and the quiz suggests the right ballet or jazz level and books a placement class."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 5. Needs the studio's level descriptions and the owner's placement rules. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Dropped-dancer win-back
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Families whose dancer stopped mid-year get a note before fall registration with a returning-dancer offer."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 6. Needs last season's rosters and who dropped.

softwareAI.name: Recital FAQ bot for show week
softwareAI.pitchLine: "During recital week, parents ask the bot about call times, hair and makeup rules and pickup, and it answers from the recital hub."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 5, a few weeks before recital. Needs the recital packet. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Class video portal for home practice
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Dancers log in and watch their own class's recital dance, so practice at home matches the choreography."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 6. Needs teacher-recorded videos per class and parent consent for any dancer shown.

softwareAI.name: Dancewear and recital merch shop
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Recital shirts, studio jackets and dance bags ordered online before the deadline, with one order list for the printer."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 6, ahead of recital. Needs the product list, sizes and printer deadline.

softwareAI.name: Enrolment forecast for next season
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Before the schedule is set, the owner sees which dance classes are likely to overfill or run thin, based on this year's rosters and re-enrolment."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 9, after a full season of registration data. Needs rosters and re-enrolment history. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Productise the recital hub and costume tracker for every dance studio
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "I built a recital hub and costume tracker for one dance studio. Every studio owner runs recital season off the same spreadsheet."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Recital season is the same pain at every studio, and owners compare notes at every competition weekend.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Offer every member dance studio a registration-ready site template with syllabus levels built in, as a membership benefit."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Associations sell certification and need renewals. One deal reaches many studio owners who already trust them.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Studio finder for a costume manufacturer
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Your catalogue goes to every dance studio. A recital planning tool for studios that order from you keeps them ordering every spring."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Costume companies compete for the same studios every year, and a tool the studio relies on beats a discount code.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Registration and results pages for dance competition producers
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Every stop on your dance competition tour needs entries, schedules by routine and results. One platform for the season, from someone who builds for studios."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Producers run many weekends on the same format, so one build pays back across the tour.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Each dance studio location gets its own class schedule and recital hub on one shared template. I build it once and roll it out."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: One contract becomes several locations, and group owners already budget for local pages.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: White-label dance studio template for agencies
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Your agency gets dance studio clients and builds from scratch. License my enrolment template with class levels and the recital hub built in."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Agencies sell the client; you sell the dance-specific part you've already perfected.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Community theatre audition and class pages
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Your youth theatre classes and audition sign-ups need the same registration flow I built for a dance studio across town."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Theatres share families and teachers with dance studios, and their audition seasons need online sign-up.

routesToBiggerBuyer.whoPays: A group of auditoriums or a school district facilities office, annually
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Every dance studio in the region hunts for a recital stage each spring. One booking page for your auditoriums fills the weekends."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Districts and venue groups rent the same stages to many studios. The studio client knows exactly how painful booking is.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Your gyms sell classes by age and level with a showcase every spring, the same shape as a dance studio. My template fits."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: The enrolment and showcase pattern carries over, and the finished dance site is proof.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Dancewear chain studio dress code directory
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Parents walk in asking what their studio requires. A dress code directory for every dance studio you serve sends them to your stores."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Chains sell on dress codes but keep them on paper behind the counter. Studios happily share them.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: The same dance studio stack in the next metro
routesToBiggerBuyer.whoPays: New dance studios in a new metro
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Once one ballet and hip hop studio in {City} is live, I take the recital hub and registration template to studios an hour away."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Non-competing geography lets you reuse the template, the pitch and the finished dance proof.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Rescue stalled dance studio software setups
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Someone half-set-up the studio's registration and parent portal and vanished before fall. I can finish it on a setup I've run for another dance studio."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Stuck owners already decided to buy and have a hard registration deadline.

upsellLadder.offer: Dance studio site build plus care plan, one contract
upsellLadder.trigger: They say yes to the demo.
upsellLadder.line: "The dance studio site and the care plan go on one contract, so a new season's schedule is an email to me, not a weekend for you."

upsellLadder.offer: Online registration with sibling and multi-class pricing
upsellLadder.trigger: They mention the front desk working out multi-class discounts by hand.
upsellLadder.line: "Two dancers, four classes, one sibling discount. Let registration do that maths instead of the front desk."

upsellLadder.offer: Trial dance class follow-up and review requests
upsellLadder.trigger: A month of trial class bookings shows children who tried one dance class and never registered.
upsellLadder.line: "Those trial dancers loved class. Let's follow up that evening and ask happy parents for reviews."

upsellLadder.trigger: Costume orders are being placed and some families haven't paid.
upsellLadder.line: "Costume deadlines are coming. Let the reminders chase the fees so the front desk doesn't have to."

upsellLadder.trigger: They announce the recital date and venue.
upsellLadder.line: "Recital is booked. Let's sell tickets online with seating so nobody queues at the studio on ticket day."
